MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JULY 10, 2019

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, July 10, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:03 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Chairman Larry Springs
Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Terry Coleman

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Art Salazar, Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that staff received notification from
Commissioner Coleman that he would not be attending tonight’s
meeting and staff received one item of written communication
regarding Item 6b, copies have been placed at each of the planning
commissioners seats and copies have been placed at the lobby table,
for the public.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to approve the minutes of
December 5, 2018 and was second by Commissioner Rice.

MOTION:

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, Trejo and Chairman Springs.

Commissioner Rice made the motion to approve the minutes of January
9, 2019 and was second by Commissioner Holly.

MOTION:

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, Trejo and Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-006 (SP-2019-006) AT 132 SOUTH
MARKET STREET. A public hearing to consider an application by Brion
Moran, representing The Dime, for Special Use Permit No. 2019-006 (SP-
2019-006) to allow an approximately 2,500 square-foot bar with on-site
sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits, indoor live entertainment,
and outdoor patio dancing located on the first floor of an existing two-
story, two-tenant 3,500 square-foot commercial building on a 4,625
square-foot H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 132 S. Market Street.

Ms. Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner, made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Holly stated he would save his question for the
applicant.

Commissioner Rice asked staff-
 Would the roll-up door on the south-side of the building extend
  the active footprint of the property out onto the grass areas?
  - Ms. Kay stated yes, and that the applicant proposes two
  outdoor dining areas, one along the market street frontage
  and one along the adjacent parcel, which would require a
  design review and they would have to come back at a later
  date for the exterior modifications and then it would have to
  require some type of agreement with the City to use that land.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff-
 Are you talking about a front patio, a back patio and now a side
  patio? I’m looking at the plans here in the staff report and it
  looks like a side patio.
  - Ms. Kay stated yes, on the plans it shows a recessed patio
  area on the back, but that’s not proposed to be used for
  outdoor dining.
 As I’m looking at the staff report I see you have outdoor dining
  but also outdoor dancing, would you show where the outdoor
  dancing will take place?
  - Ms. Kay stated it will be in the general area in the
  approximate walkway slightly adjacent to the tables where the
  layout is shown on the floor plan.
 How will it be outdoor dancing, will there be a platform or
  flooring for the dancing?
  - Ms. Kay stated no, it’s just when people are outside when the
  music is playing at a level to where the people can do a
  little dance move...
 Now that brings me to the 42” metal fence, which is only about
  3.5 feet, how will it prevent anyone from jumping over the wall,
  because they see people outside dancing, it’s next to the
  parking lot, it looks like fun and they want to join in?
  - Ms. Kay stated that the primary entry for patrons will be the
  front entrance, so all guests of the bar would have to enter
  through the front at Market Street, so if someone is
  interested in entering the bar, that is where they would have
  to go. Now there will be security guards positioned so that
  in the event anyone tries to go over the guardrail they will
  be stopped.
 Is there any visibility from the indoor to the outdoor, because
  what I saw was a solid wall unless I’m misreading it?
  - Ms. Kay asked on what portion of the building?
 Where the outdoor dining is on the walkway
  - Ms. Kay stated that on the south there is a proposed roll-up
  door and that design is pending, because it still has to go

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
  through design review, so as shown presently it does have
  glass openings, where you would be able to see into the
  interior when you go back to this concept they are like the
  modern style glass rollup door, but that is not the final
  design for that could potentially be where you can see into
  the interior of the building.
  I’m talking about seeing what’s in the exterior – the applicant
  will have people eating and drinking outside, people dancing
  outside, how will the staff be able to look at what’s going on
  from the inside – on that side of the patio – and it’s just an
  additional level of security, but how will staff be able to see
  what is going on – in that area of the patio?
  - Ms. Kay stated there are Security personnel and the applicant
  could speak to this with greater detail, but in the additional
  location both staff and security circulate throughout the
  facility during hours of operation to make sure that all
  patrons’ behavior is monitored.
  She stated that she feels there needs to be more visibility to
  that side patio area so that nothing negative can occur, as it
  could have been prevented with a greater security presence and
  more visibility, also there is a large parking lot and there
  will be nothing that can be done regarding the parking lot and
  those that will be utilizing it, but if there are people
  celebrating, what is the barrier that will protect the patrons
  who could possibly be sitting outside in that patio area, is
  what my concern is for more security for the patrons.
  - Ms. Kay as the applicant has proposed the back patio is not
  to be acceptable to any of the patrons at the bar at all, but
  is to be used as a back service entry and access for staff of
  the bar and the upstairs tenants.

Commissioner Rice asked staff-
 About the south side of the building, with a 42” fence all
  around the entire perimeter of the building, except it’s
  enclosed, with the only opening coming from the south-west side
  of the building where the applicant and patrons enter, is that
  correct?
  - Ms. Kay stated yes, as there is no other pedestrian access to
  the bar or the bar’s patio, except through that entry on the
  west.
 His concern is should there be a fire or emergency at that
  entrance, which might occur, how would the patrons get out if
  they could not jump 42” off the ground, how would they exit the
  area safely?
  - Ms. Kay stated that there will be a security and evacuation
  plan submitted by the applicant during the site plan review.

Chairman Springs asked for the applicant to come forward to address
the planning commission.

Mr. Brion Moran, Architect and representative for the applicant
along with Mr. Andrew Fiscella - owner of “The Dime” Restaurant.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
ask questions of the applicant.

  -  Mr. Moran, Architect and representative for the applicant
  came before the Planning Commission to state what the benefits
  to the community will be with this new venture and project
  here in the City of Inglewood, and where they will be located
  on Market Street.
  -  Mr. Andrew Fiscella, property owner came to address some of
  the answers to Commissioner Trejo’s questions regarding
  security for both their patrons and staff. He also spoke about
  how they will encourage their staff and patrons to order food
  from the local restaurants in the area.

Commissioner Holly asked the applicant:
 With regards to the security cameras on the premises, would the
  applicant be willing to link the cameras to the Inglewood Police
  Department, for the protection of both the staff and the patrons
  with a live-feed so there will be the opportunity to assist the
  applicant’s establishment immediately should the need arise.
  - Mr. Fiscella stated that will not be a problem, as his father
  was a policeman, and he will insure to have a live-feed to
  the local IPD.
  - Mr. Fiscella also addressed the questions regarding dancing
  and partying on the outside of the building, and stated that
  although they will run a fun and enjoyable operation, and
  will not keep people from celebrating the various victories
  they will be enjoying, they will monitor such activity in
  order to make sure the sounds of celebration do not surpass
  the noise decibel requirements.

Commissioner Rice stated to the applicant:
 How he wanted to thank the applicant for coming to the City of
  Inglewood to bring some spice to the community and to liven the
  area up and he looks forward to this new project.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 She also wanted to acknowledge the applicant and thank him for
  bringing this new project to the City. She stated that she sees
  that Mr. Fiscella is willing to insure security and safety to
  both his staff and the patrons that will be at his establishment.
 She asks if this is the second (2nd) business location for the
  applicant?
  - Mr. Fiscella stated yes, it is and stated that his previous
  establishment has little to no major police incidents that
  have caused any severe bodily injury to either his patrons or
  staff, as they are very cooperative with the local
  authorities.
 She asks about page six of the staff report where it talks about
  the applicant and his request for an outdoor dining permit, and
  how he proposes to install a new roll-up door and proposes to
  offer access to the second-floor, also “should the applicant
  decide to proceed”, this statement sounds indecisive, as if the
  applicant might or might-not actually do what is proposed, and
  the question is will the applicant do these actions or not?
  - Mr. Moran answered with the statement that it all depends
  upon the building to be structurally sound. Also if it is
  cost effective and structurally sound, and if the applicant
  is allowed to have an all-glass wall, which the applicant
  would be more than thankful. In regards to the staircase, it
  is an internal issue that the property landlord is helping
  the applicant with, because of the front egress of the
  staircase and since the placement is where the bar is
  dedicated to be.
  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
  -  Mr. Moran also stated that it would give a very pleasing
  effect with having a great visual of the outside with an all
  glass roll-up door, where you would also have the ability to
  keep the noise inside, and yet have a great event indoors.

Commissioner Trejo made a statement to the applicant:
 If she is not sure what is being proposed and brought before
  the planning commission, then they are not sure of what the
  complete picture or project is intending to be, therefore it is
  easier to see exactly what is being proposed if the applicant
  would take the time and spend a few extra dollars for at least
  a rendering and a displayed layout, it would give the full
  picture of what is intended to be which will be a great benefit
  for the City, but pays off for the applicant in the end.
  - Mr. Fiscella stated that what is being proposed is exactly
  what is planned for the site. Although there are no building
  plans as of yet, it is exactly what is the intent. Until there
  are building plans that approve any structural issues, this
  is what we would like, to add more windows along the patio
  area, per your comments, it’s just at this point we haven’t
  gotten to the point of submitting with Building and Safety
  for structural approval and so that is our next step.
  - Ms. Wilcox wanted to address the commissioners that this
  request is just for a special use permit for the Alcohol
  sales, outdoor dining and outdoor dancing and they will have
  to return to the planning commission for the exterior
  modifications that they are proposing such as the windows
  outside and any changes the applicant makes to the outside,
  so they will have to return once they have finalized the
  designs, and this is what is currently proposed.
 Yes, this is exactly the concern. That if the applicant does
  not get approved by the Building Department, that what will be
  their next step look like? For the windows and the roll-up door
  is planning commission approving Alcohol sales, the outdoor
  dining and outdoor dancing, live entertainment for a building
  that will be basically isolated from the outside. What is
  presently being displayed, may not receive approval as planned
  by the Building Department and then the project that will be
  built, may be totally different.

Chairman Springs interjected:
 That at this present point, he is certain that the applicant
  will make sure to meet and work with staff to insure that their
  proposed ideas will be approved by the Building Department, and
  that the applicant’s project will move further to secure all
  approvals.
 He also stated that he had a few more questions for the
  applicant. Regarding the various menus of the different
  restaurants in the area, will there be great eats from these
  local eateries?
  - Ms. Lucy Treadway, Business Partner and Spouse of Mr. Fiscella
  stated that they have already been in the community making
  connections with all of the local and nearby eateries securing
  menus from Dulan’s Soul Food Restaurant to Stuff I Eat .
 What is the age limit that will be allowed in the Dime
  Restaurant? Will seniors and well-seasoned customers be
  welcomed?
  - Mr. Fiscella stated that all adults over 21 will be welcomed
  to the establishment, just like at the other location in Los
  Angeles.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the community to speak for
or against this project.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
FOR
 Mr. Marvin Virgin – Inglewood Resident
 Ms. Tracey Shields – Inglewood Resident, Business Owner
 Mr. Jeff Arnold – Security Officer of The Dime @ Fairfax

Chairman Springs closed the segment for/against this project and
opened last remarks from the Planning Commissioners.

Commissioner Trejo:
 Looking for great diversity in businesses here in Inglewood
  and she stated she feels that The Dime will definitely fill
  that desire.
 Major concern is that this business will be a success.

Commissioner Rice:
 Just wanted to reiterate the Online Real-Time Video feed to
  Inglewood Police Department, as it is imperative, a definite
  must.

Commissioner Holly:
 It was a great presentation by staff, and the applicant and
  looking forward to the start of something wonderful here in
  Inglewood, welcome to the City of Inglewood.

Chairman Springs called for a motion from the Planning Commission
for this project.

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-053 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2019-006, subject to 33 conditions and was second by
Commissioner Holly, Resolution No. 1841,

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR BRION
  MORAN (REPRESENTING THE DIME) TO ALLOW AN
  APPROXIMATELY 2,500 SQUARE-FOOT BAR WITH 1)
  ON-SITE SALE OF BEER, WINE AND DISTILLED
  SPIRITS, 2) INDOOR LIVE ENTERTAINMENT, AND 3)
  OUTDOOR PATIO DANCING LOCATED ON THE FIRST
  FLOOR OF AN EXISTING TWO-STORY, TWO-TENANT
  3,500 SQUARE-FOOT COMMERCIAL BUILDING ON A
  4,625 SQUARE-FOOT DOWNTOWN TOD PLAN, H-C
  (HISTORIC CORE) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 132
  SOUTH MARKET STREET.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, Trejo, and Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

There was a 10 minute Break to allow for the next applicant to set
up for Item 6B.

Chairman Springs called the Planning Commission Meeting back to
order at 8:02p.m.

6B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-007 (SP-2019-007) AT 348 WEST ARBOR
VITAE STREET. A public hearing to consider an application by
Shanita Nicholas, representing Sip & Sonder, for Special Use Permit
  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
No. 2019-007 (SP-2019-007) to allow an event center with live
entertainment and the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption
within a café on a 3,742 square-foot, H-C (Historic Core) zoned
property at 348 West Arbor Vitae Street.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 ABC Licensing has a census-tract that states there is an over-
  concentration of facilities with liquor licenses in the area
  and could staff repeat it for clarification.
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes - that ABC Licensing stated that in the
  area after two like businesses wanting to have Beer & Wine
  Licenses would constitute as over-concentration.
 Then is it true that in the area already there are nine (9) such
  active licenses?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes – that eight (8) of the nine (9) are
  sit-down restaurants.
 There was one (1) crime at the subject site, what type and when
  and was the site vacant?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, in 2017 per information from Inglewood
  Police Department (IPD), burglary at that address.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Per the IPD stating that there was one crime incident in 2017,
  and none in 2016 or in 2018, was Sip and Sonder operating at
  the time of the burglary? And if not, what type of business was
  operating?
  - Ms. Fewell stated Sip and Sonder were not operating at the
  time, but another establishment was present, a food market
  was occupying the location and there was no sale of beer
  and/or wine at that time.
 Once they obtain a license from ABC, should the applicant be
  approved by this planning commission, will the future new
  tenants have to follow the rules and agreement ordered by ABC?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, no more beer and wine licenses will be
  allowed in that area due to over-concentration, with the PCN
  finding, and it will be recorded with the County of Los
  Angeles, enforced and will have to be followed by all tenants.
 With regards to special events at the site, will the applicant
  have to go before the permits and licensing board in order to
  be approved for every event or will it be one blanket approval?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that it is a blanket approval.
 Per the staff report, it states for the special events that are
  to be held, “…a small number of attendees will be present”, but
  “a small number” is not truly defining as to the number of
  attendees, and so before giving a blanket approval for special
  events, I would like to have a better definition as to the
  number of expected attendees.
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant is present this evening
  and would be better able to speak to this question.

  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019

Commissioner Coleman commented to staff –
 Regarding the adding of one more security camera – to capture
  the front of the establishment and also the addition of staff,
  especially for special events, it increases safety for all.

  All other questions will be for the applicant.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
the planning commission.
Both Ms. Amanda Jane Thomas and Ms. Shanita Nicholas, co-owners of
Sip and Sonder Restaurant addressed the planning commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for questions to the applicants
by the planning commission.

Commissioner Holly asked –
 For the applicants to speak to the planning commission as to
  how the community has come out to embrace the business since
  its initial opening and how there has been an increase in revenue
  as well as community participation.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that it has been an increase that far
  exceeded her expectations in a very short amount of time. The
  fact that a great deal of the community loves the idea that
  there is a great space they can just walk to meet friends
  anytime of the day and not only customers from within the
  immediate area have been coming during the day/lunchtime, but
  in the early and also late evenings to meet and greet with
  old and new friends, co-workers and possible clients. The
  repeat customer fan base has truly been enjoyable to see how
  often they will come to sit and enjoy not only the atmosphere,
  but just a cup of tea or coffee.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that several of the new clients have now
  designated Sip and Sonder as a safe meeting space for their
  gatherings which ends up being an all-day session, one in
  particular, the Women’s Writing Group from USC. This is more
  than just a coffee shop, it is being utilized as a “space”
  where many things can take place. There are some that come
  because they need a mid-space to meet between distances from
  Long Beach and Downtown L.A., and so they utilize the space
  here. Also this is a space where customers can take and make
  phone calls to complete various projects.

  Other than having an open space where different people can come
  for coffee, or recordings or other types of programs, are there
  projects or events for the community that only you offer?
  - Ms. Thomas stated that both she and Ms. Nicholas are Attorneys
  at Law, and this requires them to conduct a higher standard
  of diversity and inclusiveness of all members of society. She
  stated that they do operate and are lead for a non-profit
  organization that meets at Sip and Sonder. The L.A. Black
  Investors Club non-profit assists with various Women
  organizations and many groups by offering self-motivating
  talks and sessions, also various communities are impacted by
  this non-profit. One of the members of the L.A. Black
  Investors Club gives talks on starting small businesses,
  which helps many to see the possibilities available to them.
  Along with the recordings and videos made, the space offers
  a great atmosphere for more than just coffee lovers.

Commissioner Rice stated:
 He was able to visit Sip and Sonder recently, and found it to
  be a very pleasant place and wanted to say thank you for bringing
  this project to Inglewood and welcome.
  8
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019

  He stated that various businesses here in Inglewood make sure
  their customers have food present along with the selling of Beer
  and Wine, and wanted the applicants to inform the planning
  commission on the various food choices that will be and are
  being sold now at Sip and Sonder?What benefits to both Sip and
  Sonder and the community will take affect with the selling of
  Beer and Wine?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated currently in our coffee shop there are
  sweet and savory snacks, pastries and small food items, pre-
  packaged sandwiches that are available for purchase, and
  since at present there is not a full working kitchen these
  current food items pair very well with our coffees, juices
  and teas. With the various current events that will be taking
  place such as our open mic and spoken word evenings, and when
  the Beer and Wine approval happens, our arrangement is to
  partner with several food delivering services as well as
  connect with some of the local full kitchens, so that there
  will be the same food continuity with the Beer and Wine that
  is here now with the coffees and teas.
  - Ms. Thomas stated that they guarantee to continue having this
  outsourced feature with bigger and better selections, as it
  is important that their customers will be serviced fully with
  healthy food options.

Commissioner Trejo asked:
 Are there events happening at Sip and Sonder now?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that just the past month, there was a
  small “Open Mic” night, as there happened to be around 15 to
  20 people who extended their stay from the late afternoon
  arrival and so with that size in attendance, and it ended at
  10:30pm which extended the operating hours.
 Where did the patrons park during the extended hours for the
  Open Mic night?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that the parking structure around the
  corner on Locust is open and operating, along with the patrons
  that stayed from the afternoon who parked on the street and
  those that arrived after 6:00pm.
 What do you feel makes Sip and Sonder a unique business model
  and  therefore  provides  for  public  convenience?  Public
  Convenience has to be made because there is an over-
  concentration of liquor licenses. Please describe your business
  model.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that as it was eluded to earlier that the
  community has come out and supported this business because
  this is the type of place they have been looking for where
  they can come, greet and meet not only old friends but new
  friends, in a space that will allow them the opportunity to
  be free to enjoy their day and evening at a nice pace, where
  they can literally just sit, sip, and sonder the day’s events.
  It is an environment where the community has spoken to how
  they thoroughly enjoy being able to come into Sip and Sonder
  and just relish in the way they are pampered and served. We
  are confident that this environment will continue to grow.

Commissioner Trejo made a statement and then asked:
 At her daily job, her co-workers know that she lives in
  Inglewood, and several weeks prior to the Planning Commission
  they asked where in Inglewood are the new places to eat and just
  enjoy themselves, so she looked up “new places in Inglewood”
  and found Sip and Sonder. She looked at the website and read
  the manifest and found that only a certain demographic was being
  targeted, the website appears to be non-inclusive of all of the
  different cultures that live in Inglewood and feels the answer
  needs to be heard and asked Ms. Nicholas and Ms. Thomas to
  9
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
  explain why they appear to be targeting just one group of
  people?.
  - Ms. Thomas stated that although it may feel that Sip and
  Sonder’s website is only targeting the African American
  community, we targeted this culture because there are not
  many if any of these types of culture driven places where
  people of color could come and enjoy their heritage proudly.
  Although there are many cultures represented in the City of
  Inglewood and our website does speak to the African American
  community, it’s for that very reason that it speaks to all
  diversities and is very inclusive of all. This was part of a
  review that was posted on “YELP”, within the first weeks of
  opening and it feels very true to me still to this day.

  -  Ms. Nicholas stated that within any organization and business
  that has a goal or mission of some sort, there is a base
  target that matters to the business and what in particular
  they are aligned with, mainly it’s the audience that becomes
  the mission of the business to try to aim for and reach. Sip
  and Sonder is definitely for the community and the culture
  that is Inglewood. The response and statements that we have
  received from those in the community who continue to come
  back to Sip and Sonder speak to the diversity and feel of a
  place that is inclusive for all. This is a great feeling that
  should be continued and celebrated.

  -  Ms. Nicholas stated that with the diverse staff and members
  of Sip and Sonder, it is a “space” that takes on the persona
  of those that work there - in that space - and the pride that
  they have in serving the clientele, both repeat and new.

Commissioner Trejo asked one more question about
 What does small number represent and especially for the 2:00am
  events, as one person’s version of small may be fifteen, others
  may see small as two.
  - Ms. Thomas stated that the initial desire for the use of the
  space was to not limit the length of a performance, thus
  allowing it to continue until completion. The time of day was
  just a number given, but not intended to always end at that
  time.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated the times listed were what they were
  receiving from the community. If there was a plan to stay
  open late in the evening, Ms. Nicholas stated they would close
  early around 2:00pm and then open back up in the early evening
  such as 6:00pm until around the conclusion of an evening’s
  performance. She stated that the customers requested that if
  Sip and Sonder would be closed on certain afternoons, if it
  were possible to post when Sip and Sonder would be closed in
  advanced and when it would be open and to pick particular
  days and evenings for these performances and so in order to
  not limit the closing time that particular time was chosen in
  order to ensure all performances would have the adequate time
  needed.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 One important fact that will be reinforced and that is the
  serving of beer or wine must be accompanied with food. There
  are the dangers of one glass of wine and one glass of beer
  leading to two and to have people full of alcohol and nothing
  for them to eat can’t be allowed. So if this SUP gets approved
  that will be a definite condition that will be voted into
  approval.

  10
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 10, 2019
Commissioner Coleman thanked the audience and the applicant for
